resources.string: A clear view of device trust
Requests su authorization from Magisk, KernelSU or APatch. Does not disable SELinux or modify system partitions or APEX.
Visibility depends on system permissions. Try refreshing, granting root or opening system settings.

Only certificates actually read are shown. Other users, locked work profiles and vendor stores may be inaccessible. Counts are not a complete device inventory. A file alone does not establish active trust.
System CAs support viewing, backup and export. Manage trust in system settings.
Store file only · active trust unconfirmed

This environment requires removal in system settings. Select the certificate and check its fingerprint. The app checks again on return. The backup is retained.
Backups stay in private app storage and are deleted when the app is uninstalled. Export backup archives to keep a copy. System CA backups are export-only. Restore within the original Android profile.

Installing a CA changes trust in this profile. Only install certificates from trusted sources.

Android 11+: choose where to save the certificate, then select it under Security → Install a certificate → CA certificate. Return to check its fingerprint. Backups are retained on cancellation or failure.

Certificates and backups are processed locally. No network permission or uploads. Logs contain only command types, times and outcomes.
Counts reflect certificates actually read. System trust anchors, disabled records and module copies are kept separate. Expand coverage for each source.
The goal is actual user CA removal. No hiding HyperOS warnings, service hooks, modified checks or disabled SELinux. A scan cannot prove the system warning has disappeared.
